scientific_use: Run quality control and filter low-detection genes, compute mitochondrial QC covariates, normalize counts to 10,000 per cell and log transform, select 2,000 highly variable genes, regress out total counts and mitochondrial fraction on a scaled layer, compute PCA and a neighborhood graph, embed with UMAP, and cluster cells with Leiden. The tutorial then supports marker-based cluster interpretation and comparison to known PBMC cell types.
tool_role_basis: The notebook composes Scanpy APIs (filtering, normalization, HVG selection, regression, scaling, PCA, neighbors, UMAP, Leiden and plotting); it does not implement those algorithms.

title: Select variable genes and cluster PBMCs with analytic Pearson residuals
repo_revision: GitHub main SHA unresolved; inspected current rendered documentation on 2026-09-29

sources.locator: Background; Download data; Perform Quality control; Use Pearson residuals for selection of highly variable genes; Transforming raw counts; PCA/t-SNE and neighborhood graph/Leiden, retrieved rendering lines 288-664

scientific_use: Compare analytic negative-binomial Pearson-residual feature selection with known PBMC marker genes, then transform raw UMI counts to residuals and use PCA, t-SNE, a neighborhood graph and Leiden to inspect cell subpopulations. The workflow runs the same analysis on PBMC3k v1 and PBMC10k v3 and preserves raw and square-root normalized layers for interpretation.
tool_role_basis: The tutorial uses Scanpy experimental preprocessing, PCA, t-SNE, neighbors and Leiden APIs; model fitting and algorithms are existing package operations, not newly implemented here.

inputs.meaning: 10x PBMC3k v1 and PBMC10k v3 gene-by-cell UMI count matrices
inputs.processing_stage: filtered count matrices; before tutorial filtering

inputs.meaning: Known PBMC marker gene set associated with T cells, monocytes, B cells, NK cells, dendritic cells and megakaryocytes
inputs.processing_stage: external biological interpretation reference transcribed from PBMC3k tutorial

outputs.meaning: QC-filtered cells and genes with 2,000 selected highly variable genes per dataset
Dense Pearson-residual representation, PCA, t-SNE coordinates, neighbor graph, Leiden labels and marker overlays

dependencies: Scanpy experimental.pp, AnnData, NumPy, Pooch, SciPy, scikit-learn, igraph and pynndescent; tutorial records versions at line 317
HVG selection precedes residual transformation to reduce dense matrix memory use
Retain original counts in layers['raw'] and normalized values in layers['sqrt_norm'] before replacing X
Negative-binomial overdispersion theta defaults to 100; residual clipping defaults to +/-sqrt(n_cells); choices affect results
evidence: Purpose and residual interpretation at lines 288-300.

It also revisits QC metrics and doublet predictions on the embedding.
tool_role_basis: The tutorial applies Scanpy APIs to an AnnData object and describes biological interpretation and QC; it does not create algorithms.

dependencies: HVG selection uses batch_key='sample'; data representation choices and selected genes flow into PCA and graph construction
